title: JSONB Everything
summary: Stable business facts are hidden in JSONB instead of typed columns. The design loses constraints, joins, planner visibility, and schema review.
triggered_when: Relational entities store status, tenant, amount, or timestamps only inside documents.
recommended_alternative: Keep constrained, joined, sorted, and filtered facts in columns; reserve JSONB for sparse or provider-shaped details.

title: Partition Too Early
summary: Partitioning is introduced before table size, retention, or maintenance pressure justifies it. The team pays routing and uniqueness complexity without operational benefit.
triggered_when: A table is partitioned because it may be large someday, with no retention or pruning workload.
recommended_alternative: Start with clear indexes and retention signals, then partition when pruning, maintenance, or archive needs are measured.

title: Vector Before Lexical
summary: Semantic search is adopted before exact terms, filters, permissions, and full-text ranking are understood. The result is expensive retrieval with weak explainability.
triggered_when: A search feature jumps to embeddings while users still need phrases, names, categories, or access filters.
recommended_alternative: Build lexical search, metadata filters, and ranking first; add pgvector only when semantic distance solves measured misses.

title: Shard Without Distribution Key
summary: A distributed cluster is proposed without a distribution key that appears on hot reads and writes. Cross-shard work replaces the expected scale-out benefit.
triggered_when: The workload cannot name a tenant, account, or entity key that scopes most hot queries.
recommended_alternative: Stay single-primary or partitioned until locality is proven, then test a distribution key against real query traces.

title: Replica as Performance Bandage
summary: Read replicas are added to hide missing indexes, bad query shapes, or excessive application chatter. The root problem remains and now includes lag.
triggered_when: Slow primary queries are routed to replicas before plans, indexes, and freshness needs are reviewed.
recommended_alternative: Tune query shape and indexes first; add replicas for isolation or availability when stale reads are acceptable.

title: No Pooling With High Connections
summary: Application worker growth is handled by raising max_connections instead of controlling concurrency. PostgreSQL spends memory and scheduling effort on sessions rather than useful work.
triggered_when: Autoscaled services create hundreds of mostly idle database sessions without PgBouncer or disciplined pools.
recommended_alternative: Use bounded application pools and PgBouncer where connection churn or session count is the measured bottleneck.

title: Geo Logic Without PostGIS
summary: Spatial product behavior is implemented with loose latitude and longitude math. Correctness, indexing, and coordinate semantics become application folklore.
triggered_when: Queries ask within, intersects, nearest, or service-zone questions without spatial types and indexes.
recommended_alternative: Use PostGIS when spatial predicates are product behavior; keep core numeric coordinates only for display metadata.

title: No Restore Drills
summary: Backups exist but are not restored on a schedule. The team has no evidence that RTO, RPO, extensions, and runbooks work under pressure.
triggered_when: Operational plans mention backups but have no recent restore timestamp, owner, or validation query.
recommended_alternative: Schedule restore drills that prove data, extensions, permissions, and application smoke checks on a fresh target.

title: Arrays Over Child Tables
summary: Arrays are used for values that need identity, constraints, joins, or audit. The model looks compact while application code grows special cases.
triggered_when: Array elements need per-element metadata, ownership, history, or frequent filtering.
recommended_alternative: Use child tables for entities and relationships; keep arrays for small bounded sets read as a unit.

title: Unused Indexes
summary: Indexes remain after query paths change or were created speculatively. They slow writes, consume storage, and lengthen restore or rebuild windows.
triggered_when: pg_stat_user_indexes shows sustained zero scans for non-constraint indexes across representative traffic.
recommended_alternative: Review evidence, drop unused indexes carefully, and keep workload-backed indexes tied to known query shapes.

title: Redundant Indexes
summary: Multiple indexes cover the same leading keys or predicates without distinct workload value. The write path pays for all of them.
triggered_when: A table has overlapping btree indexes such as (tenant_id) and (tenant_id, created_at) without a proven reason.
recommended_alternative: Consolidate indexes around real query predicates, uniqueness requirements, and covering needs.

title: Vacuum Starvation by Long Transaction
summary: Long transactions hold old snapshots and prevent vacuum from reclaiming dead tuples. Bloat and wraparound risk grow while the root blocker may look idle.
triggered_when: Autovacuum is running but dead tuples grow because old transactions or replication slots hold xmin back.
recommended_alternative: Bound transaction duration, monitor xmin blockers, and separate batch/reporting work from OLTP sessions.

title: Naive Wall Clock Timestamp
summary: Local wall-clock timestamps are stored where event time or schedule semantics need explicit timezone handling. Ambiguous times create reporting and booking errors.
triggered_when: The model stores local timestamp without timezone for cross-region events, audits, or daylight-saving-sensitive schedules.
recommended_alternative: Use timestamptz for instants and model local schedule intent separately with timezone or range semantics.

title: FDW Without Pushdown Verification
summary: Foreign tables become hot paths without checking whether filters, joins, and limits execute remotely. Network transfer replaces local planning.
triggered_when: EXPLAIN output for FDW queries is not reviewed before production traffic depends on the bridge.
recommended_alternative: Use EXPLAIN VERBOSE to confirm remote SQL, constrain FDW to bounded paths, and create an exit plan.
